H1.note: mechanism: MS4A4A lowers TREM2, which impairs microglial phagocytosis, which 'exacerbates the progression' of AD. TREM2 is the chain's middle gene; its claim is the mechanism's 'decrease TREM2 levels ... impairs ... exacerbates'. The H1.1 paper also states MS4A4A limits phagocytosis directly and acts on TREM2 through MS4A6A and DAP12, which the chain leaves out

H2.note: title: the three genes 'interact to limit microglial neuroinflammation'; mechanism: when the axis is impaired, neuroinflammation 'leads to Alzheimer's disease'. ABI3 and PLCG2 join the chain only through unsigned associations, so only INPP5D can have a route

H3.note: the chain starts at APOE, but the mechanism is about 'disease-associated variants of APOE' and the cited paper about APOE4; loss of myelin 'leads to cognitive decline and exacerbates Alzheimer's disease' (progression). H3.3 is an appended APOE-AD association, not a link of the chain

findings.detail: Each gene-to-process step cites a GWAS Catalog row (rs7232, rs75932628, rs10933431) that reports only a variant-AD association; none names TREM2, phagocytosis or inflammation.
rs7232, cited for MS4A4A, is a missense variant inside MS4A6A (distance 0); MS4A4A is the GWAS Catalog's mapped gene 12.5 kb away.

The chain says APOE lowers myelination, but its only paper (PMID:36385529) compares APOE4 carriers with non-carriers; nothing says more APOE means less myelination, and the falsification (inhibit APOE, expect more myelination) tests the gene-level claim the paper never made.
PMID:36385529 links myelination to learning and memory in APOE4 mice through a cholesterol-transport drug; it never says myelination lessens AD.

The step says neuroinflammation leads to AD (onset); PMID:25792098 says inflammatory mediators contribute to progression and severity, so the H2 arm's last link rests only on the H2.3 paper's untested proposal that RIPK1-mediated neuroinflammation promotes LOAD (kind hypothesis, no weight).
H3.1 cites a CELLxGENE detection rate (APOE in 3.6% vs 2.0% of oligodendrocytes, AD vs normal donors), which names neither myelination nor any effect of APOE.
After exclusions, both causal links of H3's chain have no evidence; the hypothesis rests on one paper about an allele.
H3.2 ends at AD and H3.3 starts again at APOE; H3.3 is an appended association, not a link.
ABI3 and PLCG2 join the chain only through unsigned associated_with steps backed by STRING edges, so two of the title's three genes cannot reach neuroinflammation or AD.
The mechanism says ABI3 and PLCG2 'physically and functionally interact', but the cited STRING edge is text-mining only (experimental 0.00, database 0.00).

The run's own H1.3 review says phagocytosis of synapses and neurons 'seems detrimental in the later stages of AD' and the roles are 'complex and multifaceted'; contradicting_evidence is empty for all three hypotheses and sources.json has no contradicting citations.
decreases_amount is used on a disease (H1.3) and a process (H3.1), and inhibits on a disease (H3.2); read here as signed effects.
RNPS1 and LPIN2 got no hypothesis; the run lists them as unexplained rather than forcing a chain, which is honest.
No exclusion category for a citation that states the step for a different disease aspect (progression or severity, for a risk step); used `other`.

One review gives opposite signs for two kinds of the same node (phagocytosis of amyloid-beta protective, of synapses and neurons harmful); recorded as a supports and a refutes entry, but Statement.distinctEvidence keeps only the first item per PMID whatever its polarity, so Lean silently drops the refutation (S3 reports 1 evidence, disbelief 0).
An undirected gene-gene 'associated_with' has no natural form: assoc needs a target kind (used activity) and rel needs an RO relation the step does not state.

No kind for a STRING edge on a non-binds statement with a database channel of 0.50 (used textMined), nor for an Open Targets aggregate score (used observational: it pools genetic association and literature co-mention; curatedDb would weigh it like UniProt text).
PMID:41435829's span mixes cells in a dish, non-human primates and mice; one evidence row holds one design and the taxon list has no primate, so it is recorded as mechanistic, mouse.
PMID:41633359's abstract never names the species; taxon mouse is inferred from mouse gene symbols (Nlrp3, Zbp1) and in vivo motor and neuronal-loss phenotypes.

parent_disease covers evidence for a broader disease, but no rule covers evidence for a narrower one: PMID:41633359 states the H2.4 link for late-onset AD (LOAD), a subtype of the step's AD; kept, since LOAD is most AD.
